Andy Barr

Republican candidate for United States Senator, Kentucky · Open seat

U.S. Representative for Kentucky's 6th Congressional District

Andy Barr is a Republican who has represented Kentucky's 6th Congressional District, based in Lexington and Central Kentucky, in the U.S. House since 2013. He began his political career working in the administration of Gov. Ernie Fletcher. After Sen. Mitch McConnell decided not to seek reelection, Barr ran for the open seat and won the May 19, 2026 Republican primary, which included former Attorney General Daniel Cameron. He is the Republican nominee for the November 3, 2026 general election.

Where Barr stands

Cost of living / gas prices
Supports 'American energy dominance' and more investment in energy infrastructure, including refineries, pipelines and power plants, to lower costs. Says gas prices depend on energy supply and on 'finishing the war.'
Iran / military conflict
Says the U.S. owes it to service members who have sacrificed 'to finish the job and win.'
Data centers
Supports letting local communities decide where data centers go. Said 'Data centers don't belong in every community.'
Surveillance (Flock license-plate cameras)
Called for guardrails on the use of Flock cameras.
Energy and coal
Campaigning on expanded American energy production, including coal.
Agriculture and rural health care
Campaigning on support for agriculture and rural hospitals.
Guns and abortion
Campaigning on protecting Second Amendment rights and on anti-abortion policies.
Federal budget
Voted for a Balanced Budget Amendment to the U.S. Constitution.
Immigration and border security
Voted for bills to restart border wall construction, reinstate the Remain in Mexico policy, and hire more border agents and deploy new technology at the southern border.
Independence from Senate leadership
Says he respects Sen. McConnell's legacy but is 'my own man.'

Background

  • U.S. Representative, Kentucky's 6th Congressional District, 2013–present
  • Worked in the administration of Kentucky Gov. Ernie Fletcher
